verdict.rationale: AnythingLLM is a self-hosted, multi-user AI workspace platform with an API, so publishing an MCP server is a fair question and the axis applies. An automated probe reports an official MCP server documented at the MCP compatibility page, but the only first-party text is that page's title, "MCP Compatibility in AnythingLLM." That title is ambiguous and could describe AnythingLLM consuming MCP servers as a client rather than serving tools to external agents. missing for 10: first-party documentation that AnythingLLM itself exposes an MCP server (endpoint, transport, exposed tools), setup instructions for connecting an external agent, and independent or hands-on corroboration.
